findings.evidence: Basic.lean:84 `theorem lintegral_enorm_sub_setAverage_rpow_le_of_convex (hΩ : IsOpen Ω) (hΩc : Convex ℝ Ω)`. The new `p = 2` proof at Basic.lean:233 does `wlog hΩ : IsOpen Ω` and then calls that lemma with `hΩ`. Every ingredient of the reduction (a.e.-equal integrals, monotone diameter, ContDiffOn restricted to the interior) applies unchanged for general `p`.
findings.fix: Move the `wlog` into `lintegral_enorm_sub_setAverage_rpow_le_of_convex` and drop `hΩ` from that signature: `(hΩc : Convex ℝ Ω) (hb : Bornology.IsBounded Ω) (hu : ContDiffOn ℝ 1 u Ω) (hS : S ⊆ Ω) (hS₀ : μ S ≠ 0) {p : ℝ} (hp : 1 ≤ p)`. Here `hu.mono interior_subset` supplies the interior hypothesis. Then derive the `p = 2` lemma from it without a separate reduction.
findings.issue: The `wlog hΩ : IsOpen Ω` reduction (interior is a.e. equal to Ω via `Convex.addHaar_frontier`, `diam (interior Ω) ≤ diam Ω`, `S ∩ interior Ω`) is proved only for the `p = 2` special case. It still calls `lintegral_enorm_sub_setAverage_rpow_le_of_convex` (line 84), which keeps `hΩ : IsOpen Ω`, so the general-`p` inequality stays weaker than its own corollary.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/Measure.lean:89 `protected theorem nullMeasurableSet (hs : Convex ℝ s) : NullMeasurableSet s μ`. Basic.lean:220 `hu.continuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable hΩ.measurableSet` is the only other use of `hΩ` in the eLpNorm lemma (line 213).
findings.fix: After generalizing the lintegral lemma, drop `hΩ` here too: use `ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable` with `hΩc.nullMeasurableSet`, or apply the same interior reduction. Apply the same reduction to the line-154 lemma.
findings.issue: `eLpNorm_sub_setAverage_le_of_convex` keeps `hΩ : IsOpen Ω`. Openness is used only for `hΩ.measurableSet` in `aestronglyMeasurable` and for the lintegral lemma, and both can be replaced once the general lemma drops it. The same applies to `setLIntegral_enorm_sub_setAverage_le_mul_measure_rpow_mul_of_convex` (line 154), whose proof uses openness for `exists_measurableSet_subset_measure_eq` and for fderiv measurability.

summary: The PR removes `hΩ : IsOpen Ω` only from the `p = 2` corollary with a local `wlog` reduction to `interior Ω`, while the general-`p` Poincaré–Wirtinger lemmas it is derived from still require openness. The reduction belongs in the general lemma, with the special cases derived from it.
